skill.name: managing-relationships
skill.description: Manage GitHub issue parent-child relationships, dependencies, and hierarchy queries through GitHub GraphQL workflows and an authenticated gh CLI helper.
skill.summary: Manage GitHub issue hierarchies and dependency relationships with GraphQL-based workflows.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: The static command-execution findings are false positives caused by documented Markdown backticks or safe subprocess calls to the GitHub CLI without shell execution. The main residual risk is that the skill can perform authenticated GitHub issue relationship mutations through the user gh session.

remediation.issue: Authenticated GitHub issue relationship mutations can change repository planning data.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before add, remove, or replace operations, and display the repository, parent issue, and child issue before execution.

remediation.issue: Direct gh api graphql examples can be copied into a shell and run against the current repository.
remediation.suggestion: Label direct GraphQL examples as advanced usage and instruct users to inspect the target repository and issue numbers first.

remediation.issue: GraphQL queries are constructed with string interpolation.
remediation.suggestion: Keep issue arguments typed as integers, preserve shell=False subprocess calls, and validate repository metadata before building queries.

semantic_findings.title: Authenticated GitHub State Modification
semantic_findings.description: The skill enables Bash and directs use of a helper script and gh api graphql commands that add, remove, or replace GitHub issue relationships. These operations use the user authenticated gh session and can modify repository issue organization if run without confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code contains addSubIssue and removeSubIssue mutations, and the skill enables Bash commands that invoke them. This is intended functionality, but it creates an authenticated write-action risk.

content.value_statement: GitHub issue hierarchies and blockers are difficult to manage with the standard issue CLI. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through GraphQL-based relationship workflows.
actual_capabilities: Add and remove GitHub sub-issue relationships with a helper script.
Query parent issues, child issues, and full relationship summaries.
Show blocking and blocked-by dependency information for an issue.
Retrieve GitHub issue node IDs needed for GraphQL mutations.
Provide direct GraphQL examples for relationship operations not covered by the script.
limitations: Requires an authenticated gh CLI session with repository issue permissions.
Requires Issues and GitHub GraphQL access for the target repository.
Blocking relationships are described as read-only through the included helper script.
GitHub allows only one parent per issue and prevents circular hierarchies.

use_cases.title: Build an issue hierarchy
use_cases.description: Create an epic issue and attach feature or task issues as tracked sub-issues.

use_cases.title: Audit dependency blockers
use_cases.description: Review which issues block a release issue and which issues are blocked by it.

use_cases.title: Repair issue organization
use_cases.description: Move issues between parents and verify the final hierarchy after cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: List relationships for one issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the managing-relationships skill to show all relationships for issue 67 in the current repository.

prompt_templates.title: Create a parent-child link
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the managing-relationships skill to make issue 68 a sub-issue of issue 67, then verify the result.

prompt_templates.title: Move a child issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the managing-relationships skill to check the current parent of issue 68 and move it under issue 100 if needed.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a release hierarchy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the managing-relationships skill to design and apply a shallow hierarchy for issues 120 through 130, including verification steps.

output_examples.output: Issue 67 is a parent issue with three open sub-issues, one closed sub-issue, and no blocking dependencies.

output_examples.input: Make issue 68 a child of issue 67.
output_examples.output: Issue 68 was added under issue 67. The follow-up check confirms the child appears in the parent summary.
Issue 72 is blocked by two open issues and is not currently blocking other work.

best_practices: Confirm the current repository before running relationship changes.
Verify parent and child relationships after every mutation.
Keep issue hierarchies shallow so contributors can scan them easily.
anti_patterns: Do not use task list links when a true sub-issue relationship is required.
Do not move a child issue without checking its existing parent first.
Do not create deep hierarchies that make project status difficult to review.

faq.question: Does this skill require GitHub authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses the gh CLI and needs permissions for the current repository.

faq.question: Can it create new GitHub issues?
faq.answer: No. It manages relationships between existing issues.

faq.question: Can an issue have more than one parent?
faq.answer: No. GitHub supports one parent issue for each child issue.

faq.question: Can it manage blocking dependencies?
faq.answer: It can show blocking and blocked-by relationships. The included helper script treats blocker management as read-only.

faq.question: Does it work outside GitHub repositories?
faq.answer: No. It expects the command to run from a GitHub repository with Issues enabled.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
